summary: Configure Prometheus and Grafana observability for backend services
description:
Set up the full observability stack so that metrics emitted by the 5 Spring Boot services are scraped by Prometheus and visualised in Grafana.

All configuration files live under <infra/> and are mounted into the infrastructure containers via <docker-compose.yml>.

Prometheus scrape targets (host.docker.internal, reached via the extra_hosts gateway):
```
api-gateway          host.docker.internal:8080
user-service         host.docker.internal:8081
account-service      host.docker.internal:8082
transaction-service  host.docker.internal:8083
notification-service host.docker.internal:8084
```

All targets expose metrics at <GET /actuator/prometheus>.

Grafana is provisioned automatically on startup using files under <infra/grafana/provisioning/>:
- datasources: Prometheus at http://prometheus:9090 (uid: prometheus, default)
- dashboards: loaded from the same provisioning directory

Dashboards to create:
- API Health: request rate, error rate, p99 latency per service
- JVM Health: heap memory, GC pause time, thread count per service
- Banking Metrics: transfer count, transfer volume, failed transfers, cache hit rate
- Kafka Metrics: events published, events consumed, consumer lag

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Prometheus scrapes all backend services without errors
acceptanceCriteria.given: all 5 Spring Boot services are running locally and exposing /actuator/prometheus
acceptanceCriteria.when: docker compose up is executed and Prometheus starts
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Prometheus targets page at http://localhost:9090/targets shows all 5 jobs in state UP

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Grafana loads Prometheus as the default datasource on startup
acceptanceCriteria.when: Grafana starts and the datasource list is opened
acceptanceCriteria.then: a Prometheus datasource named Prometheus is present, marked as default, and returns a healthy status

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: API Health dashboard displays live request metrics
acceptanceCriteria.given: at least one Spring Boot service is receiving HTTP traffic
acceptanceCriteria.when: the API Health dashboard is opened in Grafana
acceptanceCriteria.then: panels for request rate, error rate, and latency show data with no No data placeholder

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: JVM Health dashboard reflects heap and GC metrics
acceptanceCriteria.given: at least one Spring Boot service is running
acceptanceCriteria.when: the JVM Health dashboard is opened in Grafana
acceptanceCriteria.then: heap memory usage and GC pause panels display current JVM metrics for that service

tasks.description: Create <infra/prometheus/prometheus.yml> with a scrape_interval of 15s and one scrape job per backend service targeting host.docker.internal on ports 8080–8084, path /actuator/prometheus.
Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/datasources/prometheus.yml> to automatically register Prometheus (http://prometheus:9090) as the default Grafana datasource on container startup.
Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/dashboards.yml> pointing to the provisioning directory so Grafana auto-loads any dashboard JSON files placed there.

Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/api-health.json> with panels for HTTP request rate (http_server_requests_seconds_count), error rate, and p99 latency per service using the Prometheus datasource.

Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/jvm-health.json> with panels for JVM heap usage (jvm_memory_used_bytes), GC pause time (jvm_gc_pause_seconds_sum), and live thread count (jvm_threads_live_threads) per service.

Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/banking-metrics.json> with custom panels sourced from application-level Micrometer counters: transfer count, transfer volume, failed transfers, and Redis cache hit rate (cache_gets_total).
Create <infra/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/kafka-metrics.json> with panels for Kafka producer record send rate, consumer fetch rate, and consumer group lag using Micrometer Kafka metrics.
Start docker compose, hit each service's /actuator/prometheus endpoint, confirm all targets show UP in Prometheus, open each Grafana dashboard and verify panels populate with live data.
